title: Samsung introduces SOCAMM2 memory module for agentic AI servers
snippet: Samsung Electronics has introduced SOCAMM2, an LPDDR-based server memory module designed for agentic AI infrastructure that requires higher performance, greater upgrade flexibility, and improved power and space efficiency. The module targets systems in which AI agents reason autonomously, create plans, and execute multiple tasks continuously, increasing the amount of data that servers must store and process.

title: China's AI giants converge on Ulanqab in race to build computing hub by 2028
snippet: China's leading technology companies are expanding domestic AI computing capacity in response to tighter US export controls on advanced chips and growing restrictions on remote computing services provided by overseas data centers. Ulanqab, Inner Mongolia, has emerged as a major AI infrastructure cluster, attracting Huawei, Alibaba, ByteDance, Kuaishou and VNET, with several large-scale projects scheduled to begin operations between 2027 and 2028.

title: Apple, Huawei, and Garmin highlight diverging smartwatch strategies
snippet: Backed by aggressive promotion from leading brands, smartwatches and fitness bands have joined Bluetooth earbuds as the highest-volume mobile peripherals outside of smartphones. snippet: SK Hynix used the Supercomputing 2026 (SC26) conference to promote MARS, a server rack design that puts memory, rather than processors, at the center of AI systems. The South Korean chipmaker argued that memory is becoming a deciding factor in how well AI infrastructure performs.

snippet: Google's tensor processing unit (TPU) has emerged as Nvidia's strongest rival in the cloud AI chip market, with annual product upgrades and growing orders placing Google consistently among semiconductor suppliers' top three customers, according to industry sources.

title: Samsung and SK Hynix align on north-south split for new chip park
snippet: Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix have broadly agreed to divide a proposed semiconductor park at South Korea's Gwangju military airport site into southern and northern sections, respectively, according to South Korean media reports. The arrangement is intended to support site planning and tenant agreements as the government works toward initial mass production in June 2030, although airport relocation, land handovers, and water and power infrastructure remain unresolved.

title: Kian Shen sees electric bus shipments hitting 1,000 in 2027
snippet: Kian Shen, Yulon Motor's chassis manufacturer, said electric bus shipments will enter a mature phase in 2027, rising to about 1,000 units from an estimated 800 units in 2026. title: South Korea eyes monthly rocket launches after 2035
snippet: South Korea expects to launch a rocket every month from around 2035 as satellite communications and national defense demand grow, prompting the government to diversify launch vehicles and increase launch frequency. Domestic companies including Hanwha Aerospace and Hyundai Rotem are expanding into rocket manufacturing, launch services, and propulsion-system development to reduce reliance on overseas space transportation services.
